title: X Feed Digest
summary: OpenAI says GPT‑5.2 helped derive a new theoretical‑physics result, underscoring continued momentum in model‑driven research.
AI tooling and workflows are accelerating: Codex workflow guidance, a major gogcli release, and new tools for web‑to‑Markdown extraction.
Video generation rumors (Seedance 3.0) point toward longer, more controllable AI video with sharply lower costs—if the specs hold.
Outside AI, the feed flagged macro/finance signals (beef inflation, QSBS trust structure) and practical consumer/app‑store tips.

items.title: @OpenAI: GPT‑5.2 physics result
items.body: OpenAI says GPT‑5.2 helped derive a new theoretical‑physics result; a preprint argues a gluon interaction once assumed impossible can occur under specific alignment conditions.

items.title: @OpenAIDevs: Codex workflow episode
items.body: OpenAI Devs teased a steipete episode on how Codex changes building workflows—prompting, iterating, and shipping faster—with the full release scheduled for Feb 23.

items.title: @steipete: gogcli v0.10.0
items.body: gogcli v0.10.0 ships a big Docs/Slides markdown upgrade (tables, tab‑aware edits, template slides), Drive upload/replace + convert/share, Gmail label deletion, and Contacts improvements.

items.title: @elbeyoglu: universal Markdown extractor
items.body: A new utility lets you prepend a gateway URL to any page to get clean Markdown (and also converts PDFs/images/audio), positioning it as a broader alternative to Cloudflare’s Markdown‑for‑Agents.

items.title: @SnorkelAI: Open Benchmarks Grants
items.body: Snorkel AI launched Open Benchmarks Grants, committing $3M to fund open‑source benchmarks for agentic AI with partners including Hugging Face, Together, Prime Intellect, and PyTorch.

items.title: @mark_k: Seedance 3.0 leak
items.body: Rumors from Chinese X claim ByteDance’s Seedance 3.0 is in a closed‑door sprint with long‑form generation, native multilingual dubbing, director‑style controls, and sharply lower costs—if true, a big jump for AI video.

items.title: @aakashgupta: M2.5 cost curve
items.body: MiniMax’s M2.5 reportedly activates only 10B of 230B params per pass, enabling much lower pricing; the thread argues the cost gap vs frontier models could reset agent economics while benchmarks approach top tiers.

items.title: @mirrorzk: ‘50B+’ China data bundle
items.body: A dark‑web post claims a 50B+ record China data bundle combining multiple historic leaks (police, e‑commerce, logistics, and more), suggesting a large re‑aggregation rather than a single new breach.

items.title: @PickAlphaAI: beef & inflation
items.body: Flags beef prices as a potential headwind to the cooling‑inflation narrative, highlighting food costs as a macro risk to watch.

items.title: @sw_lilacwealth: QSBS trust substance
items.body: A reminder for founders that QSBS multi‑trust strategies only hold up if each trust has real economic substance—distinct trustees, rules, and control—otherwise exclusions can be challenged.

items.title: @scaling_shields: card warranty claims
items.body: Highlights that many credit cards automatically extend manufacturer warranties; the thread walks through a simple claim process that can refund repairs and replacements.

items.title: @om_patel5: App Store approval checklist
items.body: A fast‑approval checklist: account deletion, no “beta/coming soon,” clear pricing, privacy policy + landing page, test credentials, proper screenshots, and pre‑submission QA.
